answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed random juries. Each participant locks a bond before it may grade, and the protocol draws a fresh, secret jury for every answer, so an attacker cannot pre-target reviewers. To sway a verdict with fakes they must register and bond every fake identity separately; the cost grows linearly with each new Sybil while their odds of filling a jury stay slim, and caught collusion slashes the stake. A pearl of bond per fake, an orchard of throwaway accounts, and a velvet sheen of legitimacy all still require real collateral.
